profile.campus: Iron Mountain Northern Virginia / Manassas campus (142 acres)
profile.reading:
Iron Mountain VA-3 is one of the operational buildings on Iron Mountain's Northern Virginia data center campus in Prince William County, Virginia, addressed in this registry as 11640 Hayden Road, Manassas. Iron Mountain Incorporated, the parent company (NYSE: IRM), is a publicly traded real estate investment trust headquartered in Portsmouth, New Hampshire whose core historical business is physical and digital records management. Its entry into large scale data center operations came substantially through the January 2018 acquisition of IO Data Centers, which brought facilities in New Jersey, Ohio, and two Arizona sites into the Iron Mountain portfolio. The Virginia campus predates that deal and has grown as its own line of business inside the company since.

Per Iron Mountain's own current locations page for Virginia, the Manassas campus totals 142 acres and, as fetched for this research, has seven data centers in operation, publicly naming VA-1 and VA-2 (VA-2 carrying the company's internal DCOS Maturity Level 3 certification) along with a rendering of a future VA-6 building still to be built. The company states combined existing and planned capacity across the campus at more than 400 megawatts and combined space at more than 2 million square feet, and separately reports having acquired an adjacent 40 acre parcel to support two further buildings estimated at roughly 150 additional megawatts. VA-3 itself is not named or described with individual specifications on Iron Mountain's own site as fetched for this research, so this registry cannot confirm VA-3's own square footage, IT load, utility service size, standby generation, or year built from a primary operator source, and none of those four figures are asserted here.

Prince William County's Board of Supervisors has approved multiple rezoning and special use permit cases for Iron Mountain expansion in this same corridor in recent years, illustrating the county's active, case by case review of this operator's growth. As one example, InsideNova reported that supervisors unanimously approved rezoning case VA 8/9 in the Brentsville District, converting just under 19 acres near Wellington Road and Sudley Manor Drive from office flex, planned mixed use, and agricultural zoning to light industrial (M-2) to extend the Iron Mountain campus, after the Planning Commission had recommended approval by a 5 to 3 vote. That case called for roughly 48 megawatts drawn from Iron Mountain's own internal substation with no new substation construction required, a maximum building height of 75 feet including rooftop mechanical equipment, and a minimum 411 foot building to building separation from the neighboring Arcadia Run apartment complex. This registry has not been able to confirm from public sources whether that particular rezoning parcel underlies VA-3 or is a separate expansion tract, so the two should not be treated as describing the same building.

Iron Mountain has also filed with the US Army Corps of Engineers Norfolk District seeking federal and state permits to expand the Manassas campus further, per the company's own January 2025 announcement, without disclosing additional building level detail in that release. No independent Uptime Institute tier certification, county building permit number, or assessor record for VA-3 specifically was located in this research session. In short, the campus level scale of Iron Mountain's Prince William County operation is well documented by the operator and by county meeting records, but VA-3's own building specific power and size figures remain unconfirmed and are deliberately left out of this profile rather than estimated from campus totals or from paywalled aggregator claims.
profile.capacity_note: Aggregator Baxtel (secondary, not operator-confirmed) describes VA-3 as the campus's third and largest building at that time, more than 165,000 sq ft, with two 48 MW data halls of 30,000 sq ft each planned, a two-story data center plus three-story office tower, and room for four more data halls; overall building MW capacity was behind a paywall on that source and is not applied here. Baxtel also lists VA-3's address as 11560 Hayden Rd, differing from and possibly superseding the 11640 Hayden Rd on file; both are recorded rather than one being silently discarded, since this registry could not independently reconcile them against county records this session.
profile.research_note: Gap-view review: secondary source (Baxtel, paywalled) describes VA-3 as having two 48MW data halls (30,000 sqft each) but explicitly does not disclose the overall building IT capacity total; summing the two hall figures would be this profile's own inference, not an operator/source-confirmed total, so it_capacity_mw is not written.
sources_tried: Reverse geocoding this rows own stored coordinates through a third party service (0.9 confidence), corroborated by a coherent street and numbering pattern across sibling VA rows
profile.community_note: The VA 8/9 rezoning case, one of several recent Iron Mountain expansions reviewed by Prince William County, required a minimum 411 foot building to building separation from the adjacent Arcadia Run apartment complex, a 75 foot maximum building height including rooftop equipment, screening landscaping, and employee only EV charging, terms typical of how the county has conditioned this operator's growth in the corridor, though it is not confirmed this specific case applies to VA-3.
profile.regulatory_note: Prince William County has approved Iron Mountain's Manassas campus growth through individual rezoning and special use permit cases, such as VA 8/9 in the Brentsville District (just under 19 acres, rezoned to light industrial M-2, roughly 48 MW served from Iron Mountain's own substation, Board approved unanimously after a 5-3 Planning Commission vote), rather than a single blanket approval. Iron Mountain has separately filed with the US Army Corps of Engineers Norfolk District for federal permits tied to further campus expansion, per the company's January 2025 release. Whether the VA 8/9 parcel underlies VA-3 itself is not confirmed.

reading.body:
Iron Mountain VA-3's power capacity is unpublished, making it impossible to assess its role in Virginia's data center infrastructure or AI compute availability from public sources.

Iron Mountain operates a four-campus data center development in Manassas spanning 142 acres with 400-plus megawatts across the Northern Virginia region. This facility is one of six separately numbered buildings on that campus. Virginia hosts 326 mapped data center facilities, but only 23 publish power specifications. Among those with disclosed capacity, the state holds 1,375 megawatts total. Without a published megawatt figure for VA-3, no estimate of rack density, accelerator count, or actual compute power is possible.

The operator describes its Northern Virginia assets as a colocation platform but has not disclosed which tenants occupy this specific building. Colocation facilities serve multiple customers rather than a single AI developer or cloud provider, which shapes how their capacity converts to actual compute deployment. Virginia's infrastructure density and proximity to major population centers make it strategically important for data center placement, but capacity constraints or gluts cannot be assessed when operators do not publish their specifications.

This facility's actual contribution to AI scaling depends entirely on information Iron Mountain has chosen not to release: power delivery specifications, certification level, IT load density, and tenant identity. Tracking unpublished facilities matters because they represent real buildings with real power draws on the grid. The gap between what exists and what is known underscores how much of the infrastructure binding AI compute remains opaque to observers outside the operator.
